definition: Intensify means to become or make stronger or more extreme.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word intensify. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know intensify should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: As the town-hall hour wore on, the questions intensified — polite curiosity hardening into cross-examination.
Pressure mounts by quiet accumulation; intensify says more — the force itself is climbing in strength, not just piling up.
Erupt is the ladder's far end: what has been intensifying finally bursts every limit at once.

Heighten means to raise the level of something you can sense — tension, awareness, color — so it registers a notch more sharply. Intensify claims more than a raised level: the force itself grows stronger and more concentrated, its own dial turning toward the extreme. Heightened is a louder notch; intensify is a hotter fire.

Deepen means to grow more firmly rooted and more deeply felt, often with less show on the surface, not more. Intensify pushes the other direction: the degree itself climbs toward the extreme, where everyone can see it. Grief deepens over quiet years; a storm can only intensify.

The dry spell began quietly in April, a few weeks without rain that farmers shrugged off as ordinary.
By June it had begun to intensify.
Reservoir levels that had eased down a foot a month now fell a foot a week, and afternoon winds arrived hot enough to crack the topsoil.
State climatologists moved the region from 'abnormally dry' to 'severe drought,' the scale's language for a force gathering strength.
The turn mattered because droughts do not simply persist; the longer one runs, the harder it presses -- dry ground heats faster, and hot ground dries what is left.
By August the governor's office was no longer asking whether conditions were getting worse, only how fast.
